title: Il mio racconto: famiglia e quartiere
summary: Week 3 capstone: family possessives, adjective agreement, questo/quello, the quartiere — then extend your self-intro

blocks.title: Uno sguardo indietro: settimana 3
blocks.body: This week you learned to talk about **famiglia** with possessives (*mio padre*, *mia sorella* — no article at the singular), to make **adjectives agree** in gender and number (*alto/alta/alti/alte*), to use **questo** and **quello** for near and far, and to describe your **quartiere** with *a/in/da*. You also learned to describe people, from looks to character — *simpatico*, *gentile*, *in gamba*. Bel lavoro davvero.
blocks.callout: This is the end of Week 3 — family, adjectives, and your world around you, all in Italian.

blocks.prompt: Which is correct: 'my brothers are tall'?
blocks.explain: Plural family words need the article (i miei fratelli), and alti agrees, masculine plural.

blocks.prompt: Tonight you're heading to Marco's place. How do you say it?
blocks.explain: da + a person = 'to/at someone's place': vado da Marco.

blocks.prompt: Type 'this park is beautiful' in Italian.
blocks.hint: parco is masculine singular — questo and bello both agree.
blocks.explain: *Questo parco è bello.* Both questo and bello take the masculine singular ending to match parco.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the whole line.

blocks.title: Family drops the article — everything else keeps it

pairs.note: Singular, unmodified family words skip il/la after a possessive. Objects and plurals keep it.

blocks.scene: Marco visits your apartment for the first time and spots a family photo on the shelf

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Bel quartiere! E questa foto, chi sono?
lines.en: Nice neighborhood! And this photo, who are they?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Questa è la mia famiglia. Quello è mio padre, e quella è mia madre.
lines.en: This is my family. That's my father, and that's my mother.
lines.spotlight: quello/quella point at people across the room — near vs far demonstratives in action.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Sembrano simpatici. E quel ragazzo alto?
lines.en: They seem nice. And that tall guy?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: È mio fratello. Abita qui vicino, in quella via dietro la piazza.
lines.en: That's my brother. He lives nearby, on that street behind the square.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Ah, conosco quella via! C'è un bar molto buono all'angolo.
lines.en: Ah, I know that street! There's a really good bar on the corner.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Davvero? Il mio quartiere è piccolo, ma mi piace molto.
lines.en: Really? My neighborhood is small, but I like it a lot.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Ma dai, è perfetto: famiglia vicina e un buon bar. Cosa vuoi di più?
lines.en: Come on, it's perfect: family nearby and a good bar. What more do you want?

questions.q: Where does the speaker's brother live?
options: Nearby, on a street behind the square

questions.q: What does Marco say is on the corner of that street?

blocks.sample: Mi chiamo Alex, sono di Toronto, e sto imparando l'italiano. Ho una sorella e un fratello, e mia madre è insegnante. Abito in un quartiere tranquillo, vicino a una bella piazza.

blocks.prompt: Il mio racconto — livello 3! Write your full self-introduction so far: your name, where you're from, that you're learning Italian, something about your family (with mio/mia — remember, no article!), and a line about your quartiere with an adjective that agrees. Complimenti per la terza settimana — la tua storia sta crescendo!
